from.place: Proof of lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange: “conjugating each arrow through the comparison isomorphisms” and “gives exactly the mate of the ambient ringed exchange”; the direct-image comparison is the counit mate normalized in the opening and named-map paragraphs of prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image.

title: Canonical derived direct-image comparison is the invertible counit mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and $u:U\to V$ a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Work on the small etale and pro-etale sites with the constant coefficient module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact derived comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $l_u=u_{\Et}^{-1}$, $r_u=Ru_{\Et,*}$, $p_u=Lu_{\Proet}^*$, $s_u=Ru_{\Proet,*}$ for the canonical derived module adjoint pairs $l_u\dashv r_u$ and $p_u\dashv s_u$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Denote their units and counits by $\eta_u^e,\varepsilon_u^e$ and $\eta_u^p,\varepsilon_u^p$. In the constant-ring identifications [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], let $a_u:A_Ul_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_V$ be the specified pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For $K\in\Dplus(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ define $b_{u,K}:A_Vr_uK\to s_uA_UK$ to be the adjoint transpose [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of
$$q_{u,K}=A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,K})\circ a_{u,r_uK}^{-1}:p_uA_Vr_uK\to A_UK.$$
Then $b_u$ is natural in $K$ and every $b_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism. It satisfies the specified normalization
$$\varepsilon^p_{u,A_UK}\circ p_u(b_{u,K})\circ a_{u,r_uK}=A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,K}).$$
Here invertibility concerns this named morphism, not merely the existence of some isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Proof, first two paragraphs defining the mate alpha_L, and named-map verification beginning "We check that the isomorphism just calculated is induced by alpha_L"; Stacks 099R (proetale.tex, section-comparison) for the geometric setting; 0B65 (categories.tex, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints) for counit normalization.

proof.text: For $K$, compose $a_{u,r_uK}^{-1}$ with $A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,K})$ to obtain $q_{u,K}$. The mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], applied to $a_u^{-1}$ and the two adjunctions in the statement, gives a unique map $b_{u,K}$ with this transpose. For $h:K\to K'$, naturality gives $A_U(h)q_{u,K}=q_{u,K'}p_uA_Vr_u(h)$. Naturality of the adjunction bijection then gives $s_uA_U(h)b_{u,K}=b_{u,K'}A_Vr_u(h)$, proving naturality of $b_u$.

source.place: Opening mate construction; naturality in the final paragraph

proof.text:
By the transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate],
$$\varepsilon^p_{u,A_UK}\circ p_u(b_{u,K})=q_{u,K}=A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,K})\circ a_{u,r_uK}^{-1}.$$
Precomposing with $a_{u,r_uK}$ cancels $a_{u,r_uK}^{-1}a_{u,r_uK}$ and gives the normalization in the statement. It remains to prove that this specified $b_{u,K}$ is invertible.

source.place: Counit normalization of the opening mate formula; Stacks 0B65

proof.text: All module-sheaf categories here are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the small skeletons in the site convention; hence they have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose a bounded-below complex $I$ of etale injectives representing $K$, and a bounded-below complex $J$ of pro-etale injectives representing $A_UK$. Exactness of $A_U$ means that $A_UI$ represents $A_UK$. The K-injectivity assertion of the same representative lemma and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] provide a chain map $t:A_UI\to J$ representing the chosen derived isomorphism; it is a quasi-isomorphism because it induces isomorphisms on cohomology. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], the two scheme inverse images are exact. Their right adjoints preserve injectives by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]. Thus $u_{\Et,*}I$ and $u_{\Proet,*}J$ are bounded-below injective complexes representing $r_uK$ and $s_uA_UK$ by their direct-image definitions.

The assertion is local on $V$. Indeed, let $V_0\subset V$ be affine open and $U_0=U\times_VV_0$. Restriction of $I$ to $U_0$ and of $u_*I$ to $V_0$ preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]; the pro-etale analogue for $J$ and its direct image is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. On either site, for an object $W\to V_0$, the restricted direct-image complex has value $I(U\times_VW)$ or $J(U\times_VW)$, equal to the direct image formed using $u_0:U_0\to V_0$. These equalities follow degreewise from [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The composition compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the restricted inverse images. The counit evaluates those same sections on the fibre product, so its restriction is the counit for $u_0$. Transposing shows that $b_u|_{V_0}=b_{u_0}$. If these restrictions are isomorphisms on an affine open cover, the cohomology sheaves of the cone vanish: a section is zero after its pullbacks to that covering and therefore zero by the sheaf axiom. Hence it suffices to prove the assertion with $V$ affine.

source.place: Paragraph beginning “The assertion is local on V”

proof.text: Now let $V$ be affine and $W\in\mathcal B_V$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. By [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], write $W=\varprojlim_iW_i$ with $W_i/V$ affine etale of finite presentation and affine transition maps. Put $U_i=U\times_VW_i$ and $U_W=U\times_VW$. Each $W_i$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Clauses (3) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] imply that $U_i$ is qcqs. The transition maps of $U_i$ are base changes of the affine transition maps of $W_i$, so are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Also $U_W=\varprojlim_iU_i$: a cone into the $U_i$ is a map to $U$ and a compatible cone into the $W_i$ agreeing over $V$; the limit property of $W$ and the fibre-product property [def-pc-fibre-product] give exactly one map into $U_W$. Fix a stage $i_0$. The overcategory of stages mapping to it is coinitial: common refinements exist by cofilteredness, and two choices agree after a further refinement equalizing their maps. Thus the same limits can be indexed over this overcategory, as in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-continuity]. The complexes $(r_uK)|_{W_i}$ and $K|_{U_i}$ are inverse images from their respective $i_0$ stages. Both inverse systems therefore satisfy precisely that continuity lemma's hypotheses. Finally $W\to V$ and $U_W\to U$ are weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability].

source.place: Affine ind-etale presentation and the qcqs/affine-transition hypotheses

proof.text:
For every stage $i$, both $I|_{U_i}$ and $(u_{\Et,*}I)|_{W_i}$ are bounded-below injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]. Their terminal section complexes agree termwise:
$$\Gamma(W_i,(u_{\Et,*}I)|_{W_i})=\Gamma(U_i,I|_{U_i}),$$
by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus
$$H^nR\Gamma(W_{i,\Et},(r_uK)|_{W_i})=H^nR\Gamma(U_{i,\Et},K|_{U_i}).$$
These equalities commute with every transition map, since on both sides it is restriction of the same section of $I$.

source.place: Middle identification in the displayed three-term comparison

proof.text:
Pullback compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the canonical global comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], on $T=W$, identify the source derived sections with $H^nR\Gamma(W_{\Et},(r_uK)|_W)$. The two applications of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-continuity] justified in step 5, and the transition-compatible equality in step 6, give the canonical isomorphisms
$$H^nR\Gamma(W_{\Et},(r_uK)|_W)\cong\varinjlim_iH^nR\Gamma(W_{i,\Et},(r_uK)|_{W_i})\cong\varinjlim_iH^nR\Gamma(U_{i,\Et},K|_{U_i})\cong H^nR\Gamma(U_{W,\Et},K|_{U_W}).$$
The outer arrows are exactly the restriction maps specified by the continuity lemma, with the first arrow inverted.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] to $T=U_W$ and $K|_{U_W}$; [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies its pro-etale target with $H^nR\Gamma(U_{W,\Proet},(A_UK)|_{U_W})$. Since the two maps in the last sentence of step 5 are weakly etale, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] makes $J|_{U_W}$ and $(u_{\Proet,*}J)|_W$ injective complexes. The direct-image section formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives
$$\Gamma(U_W,J|_{U_W})=\Gamma(W,(u_{\Proet,*}J)|_W).$$
Consequently the last cohomology group equals $H^nR\Gamma(W_{\Proet},s_uA_UK)$. Steps 7 and 8 give isomorphisms between the derived sections of source and target, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. The next steps identify their composite with $H^nR\Gamma(W,b_{u,K})$.

source.place: Final etale/pro-etale comparison and target derived evaluation

proof.text:
On the complexes of step 3, let $B:A_Vu_{\Et,*}I\to u_{\Proet,*}J$ be the underived adjoint chain map of
$$p_uA_Vu_{\Et,*}I\xrightarrow{a^{-1}}A_Ul_uu_{\Et,*}I\xrightarrow{A_U\varepsilon^e_I}A_UI\xrightarrow{t}J.$$
The degreewise adjunction respects differentials by naturality. Its localization is $b_{u,K}$: in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], take the identity resolution on the argument of the exact left adjoint and the chosen injective resolution on the argument of the right adjoint. Its displayed fraction formula says that transposition is the localized degreewise transposition, with $t$ supplying the resolution comparison. Apply this formula to the etale and pro-etale adjunctions; the localized transpose is exactly $q_{u,K}$, so uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] identifies the localized $B$ with the named $b_{u,K}$.

source.place: Named-map paragraph: resolution model for the mate

proof.text: By step 3, each $u_{\Et,*}I^r$ is injective. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-injective-acyclicity] makes $A_Vu_{\Et,*}I^r$ acyclic for evaluation on $W$. The source module-sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and has enough injectives by step 3. The target category of $\Lambda$-modules has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. Evaluation is additive and left exact because kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], applied to the identity resolution of the bounded-below complex $A_Vu_*I$, shows that its ordinary section complex computes its derived sections. The target section complex $\Gamma(W,u_{\Proet,*}J)$ computes derived sections because that direct-image complex is injective. Thus evaluating $B$ computes $R\Gamma(W,b_{u,K})$.

source.place: Named-map paragraph: acyclic source and injective target models

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] applied degreewise to $u_*I$, and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image],
$$\Gamma(W,A_Vu_*I)=\varinjlim_i\Gamma(W_i,u_*I)=\varinjlim_i\Gamma(U_i,I).$$
For $x\in\Gamma(U_i,I^r)$, the finite-stage counit in the transpose defining $B$ takes the pulled-back section of $u_*I^r$ to $x$ itself on $U_i$: this is evaluation of the direct-image section on $U\times_VW_i$. After restricting to $U_W$, $B(W)$ therefore sends $[x]$ to $t$ applied to the image of $x|_{U_W}$ under the canonical section comparison
$$\Gamma(U_{W,\Et},I|_{U_W})\longrightarrow\Gamma(U_{W,\Proet},(A_UI)|_{U_W}).$$
Here [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the restrictions of $A_UI$, and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] specifies the comparison unit. All maps commute with the differentials and with transition restrictions, because they are maps of sheaves and of complexes. This computes the actual chain map $B(W)$, including its direction.

source.place: Named-map paragraph: evaluation of the finite-stage counit

proof.text: For the filtered system of section complexes $C_i=\Gamma(U_i,I)$, filtered colimits commute with cohomology. To see this for every integer $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to $0\to Z_i^n\to C_i^n\to B_i^{n+1}\to0$ and $0\to B_i^n\to Z_i^n\to H_i^n\to0$. The resulting kernel and quotient descriptions identify $H^n(\varinjlim_iC_i)=\varinjlim_iH^n(C_i)$. It suffices to check the underlying abelian groups, since these maps are all $\Lambda$-linear. Step 11 thus says that on cohomology $R\Gamma(W,b_{u,K})$ is exactly restriction to $U_W$, followed by the canonical global comparison, followed by the resolution map $t$. The continuity lemma [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-continuity] specifies precisely this restriction, and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] specifies precisely this global comparison. Therefore this is the composite isomorphism of steps 7 and 8, not merely some isomorphism between their endpoint groups.

source.place: Named-map paragraph: passage to the filtered colimit and cohomology

proof.text: For every affine ind-etale basis object $W$ and every integer $n$, step 12 proves that $H^nR\Gamma(W,b_{u,K})$ is invertible. Both endpoints lie in $D^+$: $A_Vu_*I$ and $u_*J$ are bounded-below representatives. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-basis-derived-detection] applies on affine $V$ and proves that $b_{u,K}$ is invertible. Step 4 then gives invertibility on arbitrary $V$. Together with the naturality from step 1 and the normalization from step 2, this proves all clauses for the specified counit mate.
